newsitem.title: USA: Salomon Asset Mgmt sees Russian debt as best bet.
newsitem.headline: Salomon Asset Mgmt sees Russian debt as best bet.

text.p: Salomon Brothers Asset Management (SBAM) expects Russian debt to be one of the best performers in the emerging markets in 1997, Peter Wilby, senior portfolio manager said on Friday.
"Internationally, we love Russia," Wilby said at a Salomon Brothers luncheon. "We think Russian credit spreads are going to continue to narrow."
Wilby told reporters after the luncheon that he expects the price of Russian dollar Vneshekonombank loans to rise to about 90 cents on the dollar from current levels of 80-5/8.

The portfolio manager, who is responsible for investing in corporate high-yield securities and emerging markets debt, also said he expects that the upcoming Russian Eurobond, which began its roadshow earlier this week, will be a huge success. "We think it will be a blowout."

Although lead managers J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg have declined to comment on the terms of the deal, market expectations are for a $500 million five-year bond with spread talk now at 300 to 335 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
In Latin America, Wilby said he favors Ecuador. "We like Ecuador quite a bit. We think Ecuador represents a cheap stable slightly improving credit quality in South America."
Although he does not expect a continuation of the dramatic spread tightening seen in 1996, Wilby said he does expect improving credit quality among emerging market countries.

"We won't see another 400 basis point spread narrowing in 1997 but in a continued backdrop of strong global economic growth...credit quality will continue to improve in emerging market countries," Wilby said.
Wilby, who also manages domestic high-yield bonds, said emerging markets represent about 20 percent of the high-yield portfolios and about 20 percent of the global asset allocation bond funds.
